newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO agree to talks after untangling snag.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO agree to talks after untangling snag.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators agreed to meet on Sunday for the first time in more than two months, after untangling a last-minute snag over Jewish settlements.

Their meeting in Cairo had been cast into doubt when Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani told Reuters that Israel had in principle accepted a "pause" in settlement activities.
Israel reacted by saying it would refuse to take part in the planned peace talks until the PLO retracted the statement.
In Cairo, senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat then cleared the way for the meeting by saying Israel had not agreed to preconditions on settlement building.
"There is no agreement with the Israeli side," Erekat told reporters. He said he was not optimistic about the meeting because the two sides still had many disagreements.
"How can we have peace when Israeli bulldozers are ripping into our land and settlements are being built."
Palestinian officials said the talks would begin at 1430 GMT, half an hour later than originally planned when Israel and the PLO agreed on Saturday to revive the talks.

The negotiations have been in crisis since Israel broke ground three months ago on the 6,500-unit Jewish settlement of Har Homa on an Arab East Jerusalem hill Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim. Construction continued on Sunday.
Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu's 66-54 majority in parliament could crumble if he stopped Jewish settlement backed by religious and right-wing legislators in his government.

Israeli officials insisted that Netanyahu's right-wing government remained committed to building Jewish settlements on occupied land in the West Bank, including in Arab East Jerusalem, as well as in the Gaza Strip.
More than 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered throughout the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and home to more than two million Palestinians.
Egypt has intensified its mediation role in the three-month-old crisis since a summit between President Hosni Mubarak and Netanyahu last month.

Diplomatic sources said Egypt was pushing a five-point plan which included a freeze on any change in the status of Jerusalem and a ban on Jewish settlement building in the West Bank for "a sufficient period". In return the Palestinians would give a firm commitment to address Israel's security demands.
